research.summary: ImageMagick is a free command-line toolkit for reading, converting and editing images. In version 7 the single 'magick' program runs its tools, for example 'magick identify file' and 'magick input -resize geometry output'.

sources.title: ImageMagick: command-line options (includes -resize; 'magick' and 'mogrify' recognise each option)
sources.note: Read by the authoring session: -resize exists ('Resize an image') and its geometry argument is defined on the Image Geometry page.

sources.title: ImageMagick: identify (reports format and size of image files; 'magick identify rose.jpg')
sources.note: Read by the authoring session, including the example output line 'rose.jpg JPEG 70x46 70x46+0+0 8-bit sRGB 2.36KB 0.000u 0:00.000'.

sources.title: ImageMagick: command-line processing and image geometry
sources.note: Linked from the -resize entry; not read by the authoring session.

methods.note: ImageMagick is designed to be driven from the command line through the magick program.
MagickWand/Magick++ libraries exist but need compiled code, which this builder does not generate.

research.licensing: The ImageMagick License permits free personal, company-internal and commercial use.
limitations: Not installed on this computer: simulated tests only until it is installed.
Only PNG output and a small set of input formats are exposed.
Output files always get a new unique name; existing files are never overwritten.

decision.rationale: ImageMagick is a documented command-line program, so fixed, typed command lines are the most reliable method. No add-in, scripting engine or screen automation is needed.

commands.label: Describe an image
commands.description: Reports the format and pixel size of an image file in this project's work folder. Changes nothing.

input.description: Image file name in the project's work folder for this integration.

commands.label: Resize an image
commands.description: Makes a resized copy of an image as a new PNG file. The original is not changed. The copy is then described with identify as an independent check.

input.description: Image file name in the project's work folder for this integration.

size.description: Geometry such as 50% or 800x600 (see ImageMagick's Image Geometry page).

output.description: Name for the new image, without extension.

userGuide: Put an image in this project's ImageMagick work folder, then ask Claude to describe it or make a smaller copy, for example "Make photo.png half the size and call it small." The copy is a new PNG; your original is never changed.
